title: Compensation for material

D0.outcome: Explains what can stand as compensation for material (a lead in development, open lines, the initiative, a safer king, structure).

D1.outcome: Given a position a pawn or piece down, lists the compensation and the time it lasts.

D2.outcome: In unlabeled positions, judges whether the compensation survives the first accurate reply, and labels the verdict sound or practical.

D3.outcome: Uses engine and tablebase checks to separate sound compensation from practical chances, and says what would have to change.

misconceptions: A sacrificed pawn is a lost pawn.
Winning a pawn means winning the game (pre-engine).
conditions: A gambit is justified only if the investment buys something durable.
Give material back only for something tangible.
contrasts: A gambit-looking position where the lines are closed, so no compensation exists.
A Tal-style sacrifice that is practical but not sound and is labelled so.
A free pawn offered with no development consequence.

soft_prereq_notes.SAC.EXCHANGE.D2: the exchange sacrifice is the commonest case of compensation for material
